bands.title: Rarely worn out
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you seldom feel exhausted at the moment.

bands.title: Sometimes worn out
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you sometimes feel tired or worn out, which is common in busy periods.

bands.title: Often worn out
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you often feel exhausted. It may be a good time to look at your workload and rest.

bands.title: Very often worn out
bands.summary: Your answers suggest exhaustion is with you most of the time. Please take this seriously and look for support.

support.text: Feeling worn out often can affect your health, sleep and relationships. Consider talking to your doctor, a counsellor, or someone at work or school you trust about what could change.

personal.low: You rarely feel physically or emotionally drained.
personal.moderate: You sometimes feel physically or emotionally drained.
personal.high: You often feel physically or emotionally drained, whatever the cause.
personal.reflect: When did you last feel truly rested?
personal.tip: Protect your sleep and add short breaks to your day, even five minutes away from screens.

work.low: Your work or studies rarely leave you exhausted.
work.moderate: Your work or studies sometimes leave you worn out.
work.high: Your work or studies often leave you exhausted or frustrated.
work.reflect: Which part of your work drains you most, and which part gives you energy?
work.tip: Set a clear end to your working day and keep some evenings fully free of work.

suggestions: Burnout is about prolonged exhaustion, not weakness. It often reflects workload and conditions, not just personal effort.
Look at what you can change: boundaries, breaks, tasks you can share or drop.
Rest, movement, time outdoors and time with people you care about all help you recover.
note: Each scale is the average of its answers on the official CBI 0–100 scale (Always or To a very high degree = 100, Never or To a very low degree = 0). Your overall score is the average of the two scales. The bands follow the answer scale (25 = Seldom, 50 = Sometimes, 75 = Often) and are not clinical cut-offs. The CBI's client-related scale is not included.
